leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, Altitude Express v. Zarda, R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes v. EEOC (2020) - U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Federal workplace protection covering Arizona; discrimination on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is discrimination on basis of sex under Title VII
leads.detail: Cited as 2020 rulings that Title VII therefore protects LGBT employees from discrimination; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Arizona Governor Executive Order - January 2023
leads.documents: Bans state-based employment and contract discrimination based on both sexual orientation and gender identity
leads.detail: Signed by Governor of Arizona in January 2023; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes affirmation - June 2023
leads.documents: State law interpreted sex discrimination to include gender identity and sexual orientation
leads.detail: Affirmation by Attorney General Kris Mayes in June 2023; no URL visible in text

leads.title: Arizona Medicaid 1982 regulation and 2020 challenge; June 2023 Executive Order on gender-affirming care
leads.documents: 1982 regulation that Medicaid cannot cover sex reassignment surgery; August 2020 suit by National Center for Lesbian Rights and National Health Law Program with King & Spalding and Perkins Coie challenging as unconstitutional; June 2023 executive order giving government employees over 21 access to gender-affirming healthcare through Medicaid
leads.detail: Regulation passed in 1982; lawsuit filed August 2020; executive order signed June 2023; ACLU seeking to moot lawsuit; no URL visible

leads.title: Arizona State Legislature March 2022 bills signed by Gov. Doug Ducey - gender-affirming surgery ban for minors and trans sports ban
leads.documents: First bill legally bans sex reassignment surgery on transgender children with exception for intersex children, effective March 2023; second bill bans transgender children from female sports/athletics/Olympics, effective 30 days after enactment
leads.detail: Both passed March 2022, signed by Governor Doug Ducey; no URL visible

leads.title: Arizona Governor vetoes - June 2023 anti-trans bathroom and pronoun bills
leads.documents: Veto of bills dealing with bathrooms and banning pronoun usage within classrooms that passed Arizona Legislature
leads.detail: Vetoed by Governor of Arizona in June 2023; no URL visible

leads.title: Federal birth certificate litigation - Nov 2020 lawsuit vs Arizona Department of Health Services; Aug 2024 federal judge order; driver's license policy
leads.documents: Demand to allow change of legal gender on birth certificate without sex reassignment surgery; August 2024 order allows change without surgery; driver's license/ID change upon signed physician statement of irrevocable commitment, no surgery required
leads.detail: Lawsuit filed November 2020 by three families with transgender children; as of August 2023 ongoing; order issued August 2024; no URL visible

leads.title: Arizona Supreme Court ruling - 25 April 2019 on transgender child care
leads.documents: Family courts have authority to determine type of care a transgender child can receive in limited circumstances when parents impasse; must promote emotional/physical health, narrowly tailored and supported by imminent harm evidence
leads.detail: Case centered on divorced couple disagreeing on care for child with gender dysphoria, remanded to family court; no URL visible

leads.title: Arizona hate crime law + Matthew Shepard and James Byrd, Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act (Oct 2009) - federal law
leads.documents: Arizona includes sexual orientation as protected category with additional penalties; gender identity not included in state law, but covered federally since 2009 Act
leads.detail: Federal Act signed October 2009 covering crimes triggered by victim's gender identity; no URL visible

leads.title: Phoenix anti-discrimination ordinance and Arizona Court of Appeals June 2018 ruling; Tucson, Flagstaff, Tempe, Mesa, Scottsdale, Glendale ordinances
leads.documents: Phoenix Feb 2013 revision banning discrimination in employment, housing, public accommodations based on sexual orientation, gender identity/expression; upheld June 2018 after 2016 challenge; similar city ordinances in Tucson (1999), Flagstaff (March 2013), Tempe (Feb 2014), Mesa, Scottsdale, Glendale, Sedona, Winslow, Tolleson
leads.detail: Phoenix city council 1992 and 2013 actions; Court of Appeals upheld June 2018; no URL visible
